title: AdversarialReviewFindings
description: Output of the Reviewer agent for one implementation. The reviewer's job is to break the change: every finding must carry evidence and a refutation condition so the Implementer can either fix it or prove it wrong. 'Looks fine' is a valid result only with the checks that were actually run listed.

checks_performed.description: What the reviewer actually did. Lets a human (and the eval harness) distinguish a thorough clean review from a lazy one.

method.description: Command run, file read, or reasoning performed.

spec_conformance.description: One row per acceptance criterion in the spec.

evidence.description: Test name and result, or file:line, or the probe that was run.

finding_id.description: F-n for a reviewer's finding. DET-<check> is written only by the orchestrator, for a deterministic check it ran and saw fail.

claim.description: The defect, stated as a falsifiable assertion.

reproduction.description: Command or input that demonstrates the problem. Strongly preferred for blocking/major.

violates.description: AC ids, spec sections, or named invariants. Empty only for maintainability/nit.

refutation_condition.description: What evidence from the implementer would make the reviewer withdraw this finding. Forces the reviewer to commit to a falsifiable position.

status.description: open: new. fixed/refuted/accepted_risk: implementer's response (see review_response). upheld/withdrawn: reviewer's re-evaluation after the response.

pass.description: Which reviewer pass produced it: '1', '2', ... or 'security'. Set by the orchestrator when merging.

previous_finding_id.description: Round 2 and later: the id this finding had in previous_findings.json when it re-adjudicates one (upheld or withdrawn). The orchestrator keeps that id when it merges the passes; a re-adjudication without it is matched on category and location.

target.description: What the finding is about. `change` (the default): the product change, including a journey that would pass with the behaviour broken, since then the criterion is not shown. `verification`: only the plumbing of the factory's journey (how it reports a failure, its wording, a step it could check more tightly without changing what it proves). A verification finding never blocks the change or starts another round; the orchestrator records it in the run and the factory backlog. Post-mortem 2026-10-11 §1.

environmental.description: Set by the orchestrator on a DET-* finding whose failure looks like the verification host's doing (a port already in use) rather than the change's: the implementer answers it, but the fix is usually to make the command robust, and the judge weighs it accordingly.

cwe.description: Security findings: the single most specific CWE.

attack_path.description: Security findings: entry point -> trust boundary crossed -> sink, and the precondition an attacker needs.

exploitability.description: Security findings: how hard it is to reach the sink with attacker-controlled input from where the service is exposed.

impact.description: Security findings: what an attacker gains (data, control, availability).
